title: He was rotting… while still breathing.
paragraphs:
He was rotting… while still breathing.
And nobody would touch him.
Not even by accident.

Because some stains don’t just live on your skin.
They live in how people look at you.
How they avoid you.
How they label you.

Unclean.
Unworthy.
Too far gone.
And maybe… that’s not just his story.
Maybe that’s yours.

You learned how to smile in public…
but hide the infection in private.

The addiction nobody knows.
The thoughts you can’t silence.
The past that keeps whispering, “You’re still that person.”

You show up.
You function.
You post.
You laugh.
But deep down?
You’re asking the same question that leper asked:
“If You are willing… You can make me clean.” — Mark 1:40

Not can You.
But will You.
Because power is not the issue.
Shame is.

You don’t doubt that God is strong.
You doubt that He wants you.
And that’s where the tension lives.
That silent fear…

“What if God is holy… but not kind to people like me?”
“What if He can cleanse… but chooses not to come close?”
So you keep your distance.

You pray halfway prayers.
You confess edited versions.
You worship… but never fully surrender.
Because deep down, you think:
“If He really saw everything… He would step back.”
Just like everyone else did.
But then—
Jesus breaks the pattern.
Mark writes something shocking:
He didn’t heal from a distance.
He didn’t throw words across a gap.
He didn’t sanitize the moment.
He touched him.
That is not just kindness.
That is confrontation.
Because according to the law, touching a leper made you unclean (see Leviticus 13–14).
But Jesus does the unthinkable—

Instead of becoming unclean,
He transfers cleanness.

Instead of absorbing defilement,
He releases purity.

Instead of stepping back,
He steps in.
Let that land.

The very thing everyone avoided…
Jesus moved toward.

The very person society canceled…
Jesus embraced.

The very condition that screamed “Stay away”…
Jesus answered with “Come here.”
And then He says:
“I am willing. Be clean.” — Mark 1:41

Immediately—
not gradually,
not partially,
not conditionally—
Immediately, the leprosy left him (Mark 1:42).
This is not just healing.
This is restoration.

Skin restored.
Dignity restored.
Identity restored.
But don’t miss the deeper picture.
The leper is not just a man in history.
He is a mirror.
Because the Bible says sin does to the soul what leprosy did to the body.

It isolates.
It spreads.
It numbs.
It deforms what was once whole.
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Not some.
All.
Sin is not just what you did.
It’s what you became apart from God.
Unclean.
And no amount of self-improvement can fix that.

You can dress it up.
Manage it.
Hide it.
But you cannot cleanse yourself.
That’s why religion without Jesus becomes exhausting.
Because you’re trying to fix what only God can restore.
But here’s the Gospel turn—
Jesus didn’t just touch one leper.
He came for all of us.
On the cross, something even more scandalous happened.
The clean One became treated as unclean.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
He took the infection.

The guilt.
The shame.
The judgment.
“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
Why?
“So that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
This is the exchange.

Your uncleanness…
for His purity.

Your shame…
for His righteousness.

Your distance…
for His embrace.
But here’s where many stop short.
They admire the story…
…but never kneel like the leper.
Because the miracle didn’t begin with the touch.
It began with surrender.
“He came to Him, begging Him, and kneeling…” — Mark 1:40

He didn’t negotiate.
He didn’t defend himself.
He didn’t pretend he was okay.
He came desperate.
And that’s the doorway.
Not performance.
Not perfection.
Desperation.
Repentance is not cleaning yourself up before coming to God.
It’s coming to God because you can’t clean yourself.
And Jesus is still asking the same question without words:
“Will you come close… or will you keep hiding?”
Because He is willing.
The cross settled that forever.
So what are you doing with your shame?

Still managing it?
Still hiding it?
Still letting it define you?
Or are you ready to bring it into the light?
This is your moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you feel better.
Not when you’ve improved.
Now.

Come as you are—
but don’t stay as you are.
Let Him touch the place you keep covering.
Let Him speak over what has been screaming inside you.
Let Him make you clean.

Not patched.
Not improved.
Clean.
This is not coincidence.
This is invitation.
Type “MAKE ME CLEAN” if you’re ready to stop hiding.
